reason: Nothing found this week breaks the value/cyclical rotation thesis, and the book is already positioned to absorb the one real surprise. The 9/16 FOMC delivered a hawkish 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% (not the cut markets wanted) rather than the dovish move that would hurt cyclicals -- and that cuts for JPM (higher-rate NIM tailwind) as much as it cuts against autos. XOM's fundamentals are intact (Buy consensus, $170.91 target, only a contained Joliet refinery outage, new Angola discovery) and the leg is already +1.79%. UNH has two concrete near-term catalysts still ahead -- prior-authorization relief on ~1,700 codes effective 10/1 and earnings 10/13 -- so exiting into the current -5.39% mark right before the catalysts land would be selling the setup, not managing risk. GM and F are the legs actually under pressure from live tariff friction (GM's own $791M Ontario investment 'amid US tariff pressure' confirms the catalyst is still active), but both already carry -10% hard stops doing exactly the containment job they were sized for, with GM earnings not until 10/20 -- there is no new information that argues for overriding those stops early. The 40% cash buffer keeps compounding at 4% APY while all of this plays out, and a full seven-leg replacement would cost real bps across the book for no edge this week's research actually supports. Holding costs nothing and preserves optionality the stops already provide.
